text:
julia: Quick FYI — our Python SDK is returning inconsistent exception shapes when the service replies with 422/application/problem+json. sometimes it's ValidationError with .errors, sometimes a generic APIError with raw bytes.
sam: can you paste a repro?
julia: minimal async repro:
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient, ValidationError
client = RedwoodClient(api_key='x')
try:
    await client.chat.create(prompt='')
except ValidationError as e:
    print('structured', e.errors)
except Exception as e:
    print('fallback', type(e), getattr(e,'raw_body', None))
```
julia: result observed: `fallback <class 'redwood.errors.APIError'> b"{\"detail\": \"field required\"}"`
frank: root cause likely the async transport not running the same error JSON parser branch as sync. we used content-type checks and some infra returns application/problem+json.
sam: plan: (1) make error parser tolerant: always attempt json.loads on body with a try/except; (2) canonicalize common keys ("detail" -> errors list); (3) raise concrete ValidationError subclass (subclass of APIError) with attributes: status_code, errors (List[Dict[str,str]]), raw_body (bytes), parsed_body (str|dict). export these in typeshed.
julia: please add the quickstart snippet showing how to catch ValidationError in both sync and async flows. onboarding folks are tripping on the byte payloads.
frank: will add unit tests for sync+async error wrapping and update errors.pyi to export ValidationError/AuthError. also add APIError.is_retryable() helper for 5xx/timeouts.
ci-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/790 (py-sdk: normalize error parsing & export concrete exceptions in types)
sam: keep APIError as baseclass so old except blocks still work. add migration note in changelog: "ValidationError now consistently raised for 4xx validation failures; new attributes .errors and .raw_body".
julia: thanks — assigning to @frank, will re-check sample app when PR lands. :thumbsup:
